text:
Sam: Quick sync — we're about to migrate tenant-bound pins into the new binding-delegation surface. Concern: if runtime group A delegates a pin to pool B, what's our safety window for clients relying on model IDs? Who owns TTL renewal? :thinking:
Alex: tl;dr: owner is control plane; runtime should renew lease w/ owner token. Suggest 10m soft-window + 24h hard-evict. Need exp policy per-tenant.
Sophia: 10m seems tight for some long-lived sessions. Can we use probe-based renewal: client probes on handshake extend TTL? e.g., client sends probe every 7m -> renew.
Jess: I'd prefer a delegated-lease object attached to pin metadata: {delegate: runtime, lease_expiry: ts, renewer: control-plane/tenant}. Runtime only extends when renewer auth present.
Sam: sample metadata idea (inline): 
```
pin_metadata = {
  "binding": "tenant:xxx",
  "lease_owner": "control-plane",
  "delegate": "us-east-pool-3",
  "lease_expires": "2026-03-21T15:45:00Z",
  "renewal_policy": "probe+owner"
}
```
Thoughts?
Alex: +1 on explicit renewer. Also need fallback: if renewer unreachable, runtime should fall back to soft-evict and serve from compatible variant (not crash).
Sophia: ops question: how do we surface this in console? Need per-pin timeline + recent probe counts. Otherwise SRE will get paged.
infra-bot: deploy-plan: rolling migration. Phase1: emit new metadata without evict. Phase2: enable delegation reads. Phase3: switch renewals. We'll post the deploy manifest tomorrow.
Jess: also add audit field for who requested delegation and why (auto/manual). Helps rollbacks.
Sam: action items: Jess will draft schema PR + examples; Alex to prototype runtime fallback behavior; Sophia to add console mockups. I'll schedule 30m follow-up tomorrow. Thanks :thumbsup:
Alex: ok adding to calendar. +1
